Author_or_Organisation: Directorate of Information & Public Relations, Government of Mizoram

Author_or_Organisation: Sonowal, R.
Title: Traditional Rice Beer Fermentation Technology of the Sonowal Kachari Tribe of Assam, India

Author_or_Organisation: Bhattacharya, B.; Chandra Deka, D.
Title: Preparation, physicochemical analysis and antioxidant properties of Rohi and Sepa: traditional rice beers of the Sonowal Kacharis, Assam
Publication_or_Source_Type: Peer-reviewed article, Indian Journal of Traditional Knowledge 25(9), 914–921

Limitations_or_Caveats: Only the repository abstract was accessible in this review; Sepa-specific recipe, sampling village, and distinction from Rohi need full-text extraction. Antioxidant assay findings do not establish clinical health benefits.

Author_or_Organisation: Das, R.; Medhi, M. C.; Tamang, B.

Publication_or_Source_Type: Peer-reviewed research article, AMB Express 16, article 91

Black Rohi Modh is recorded provisionally as a substrate-associated variant pending local terminology confirmation. Antioxidant assays and predicted pathways do not establish clinical benefits.

Author_or_Organisation: Talukdar, S.; Jyethi, D. S.; Sarma, B.; et al.

It does not mention Hajang Jatha Kasa/Ruhi, Rabha Matha Mod/Roshi Mod or Tai-Ahom Luk-Lau, so it does not resolve those name leads. Medicinal or health-related claims require independent evidence.

Author_or_Organisation: Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India

Author_or_Organisation: Borah, D.; Gogoi, T.; Sarma, J.; Borah, P. J.; Gohain, B.; Mili, C.; Upadhyaya, A.; Basumatary, J.; Neog, K.; Wangpan, T.; Tangjang, S.

Do not treat its broad community-level results as village-level current-production proof; review full tables and maps before extracting specific locality or recipe claims.

Author_or_Organisation: Bhattacharya, S.; Deka, D. C.; et al. (verify full author metadata)

Communities_or_Beverages_Covered: Mech Kachari terms Haaz, Photika, Jau; starter names Haaz pitha, Zu, Bakhar

Follow cited primary sources before canonicalizing names or assigning localities.

Claims_Supported: Describes Jau/Jumai as a Deori rice beer and Photika as a distilled liquor made from it; discusses hospitality, social functions and offerings in the Deori context.
Limitations_or_Caveats: Secondary socio-cultural account with limited methodological detail and no named production village. It is useful as a cross-check because a later review also lists Jau and Photika under Mech Kachari; that discrepancy requires tracing the review citations and does not itself prove exclusive ownership or disprove use by another community.

Author_or_Organisation: Senapati, S. S.; Gurumayum, S.

Communities_or_Beverages_Covered: Traditional beverage starter cultures and plant ingredients; comparative source for checking later review citations
Claims_Supported: Reviews starter-cake preparation, fermentation practices and plant ingredients across eight named communities; useful as a separate literature trail for traditional beverage methods and plant-use claims.
Limitations_or_Caveats: Secondary review rather than village-level field survey. Do not use broad plant claims as village-specific evidence or clinical proof of medicinal effects.

Author_or_Organisation: Bhuyan, B.; Baishya, K.

Claims_Supported: Synthesizes ethnomedicinal plants and traditional rice-beer/starter information across seven named communities; secondary cross-check for beverage terminology and selected localities
Limitations_or_Caveats: Review article, not a new village census. Named places may refer to informants, cited studies or study contexts; do not infer current prevalence, universal recipes, clinical medicinal efficacy, or synonymy between similarly named beverages. Confirm locality attribution against the article text and underlying sources.

Author_or_Organisation: Deka, A. K.; Basumatary, S.; Deka, D. C.

Communities_or_Beverages_Covered: Bodo Jou/Joubidwi, stored Joufinai, Kanthal-Jougwran (jackfruit), Kola-Jougwran (banana), Kamrenga-bidwi (starfruit), Amlai-bidwi (gooseberry), Amao starter
Claims_Supported: Reports interviews with 50 people and detailed methods for stored rice-based and fruit-based Bodo beverages, including ingredients, fermentation/storage periods, local vessel names and a traditional distillation setup

Author_or_Organisation: Kumari, S.; Ama, T.; Jyoti Koch, P.; Debbarma, R.

Communities_or_Beverages_Covered: Opo starter; Nyishi rice-wine varieties named Tisar, Kecha and Adak
Claims_Supported: Characterizes physicochemical and biochemical properties of traditional Nyishi rice-wine varieties; identifies Opo as the traditional starter culture and reports sample-specific differences among Tisar, Kecha and Adak.

The abstract does not identify sampling villages or give enough evidence to decide whether Tisar, Kecha and Adak are beverage names, variety labels, or locality-specific forms.

Author_or_Organisation: Hoikhokim; Laldinthar, R.; Haokip, H.; Lhungdim, N.

Communities_or_Beverages_Covered: Anthom; sticky/glutinous rice, black or white varieties; starter called Chol; liquid fraction called aning
Claims_Supported: Documents Anthom as a fermented rice beverage and describes a source-specific process using cooked sticky rice, Chol starter, a covered vessel and fermentation for 3–7 days; the liquid fraction is called aning.
Limitations_or_Caveats: The paper reports ethnomedicinal uses as traditional claims, not clinical evidence. Village-level sampling and prevalence are not established in the accessible record; recipe and social-use descriptions should not be generalized to all Thadou-Kuki households.

Author_or_Organisation: Gogoi, P.; Konwar, S.; Das, S.; Das, D.; Doimari, R.; Sonar, T.; Doley, S.

Author_or_Organisation: Tiwari, S. C.; Mahanta, D.

Claims_Supported: Describes preparation of Apong and Ennog, starter-cake preparation and traditional equipment; interviews with elderly villagers; provides named district survey scope and named acknowledgements

Author_or_Organisation: Sarkar, Ajita
Title: Ethnobotanical studies of sub-Himalayan Duars in West Bengal and Assam with particular reference to the tribe Mech
Publication_or_Source_Type: Doctoral thesis; University of North Bengal

Communities_or_Beverages_Covered: Mech Jou/Jau rice beer; Emao starter cake; plant ingredients and source-specific preparation
Claims_Supported: Dedicated chapter 'Preparation of Jou [Rice Beer]' documents rice and five starter plants, starter-cake preparation, rice-to-starter quantities, metal fermentation vessel and seasonal fermentation duration; useful preparation-level evidence for Mech-associated Jou
Limitations_or_Caveats: Thesis is regional and does not identify an exact Assam village for the Jou chapter or establish current production. Do not equate Emao with Haaz pitha, Zu or Bakhar; does not resolve Haaz or Photika in the Mech context. Historical process description is not safety guidance.

Author_or_Organisation: Endle, Sidney
Title: The Kacháris
Publication_or_Source_Type: Historical ethnographic monograph; Macmillan and Co., published under orders of Government of Eastern Bengal and Assam
Geographic_Scope: Kachari Duars and Darrang chapter; introduction discusses northern Bodo/Kachari branch and Mech naming, but beverage passage is not village-specific
Communities_or_Beverages_Covered: Emáo starter, Zu/Záu rice beer, phatiká distilled spirit
Claims_Supported: Historical account describes starter-cake preparation, rice-beer fermentation and phatiká as a distilled spirit made from rice beer; useful comparative evidence for regional terminology and process history
Limitations_or_Caveats: The beverage chapter specifically discusses Kacharis of Darrang and does not independently establish that every Mech Kachari community used the same terms or recipe. Historical colonial ethnography with dated and evaluative language; do not treat as current practice or use it alone to equate modern Mech Photika with phatiká.
